plan.planning_summary: Refining route_04 (chirped DBR dichroic filter) based on iteration_13 results showing best_target_score ~0.919 with 20-layer HfO2/SiO2 stack. Feedback directives indicate adding gradient smoothness penalty to suppress erratic thickness jumps while preserving the coherent phase-matching structure. Three complementary routes explore: (1) smoothness-regularized optimization with chirp-constrained initialization, (2) expanded 24-layer stack for broader reflection band, (3) alternating high/low starting point to test phase sensitivity. All routes maintain parent_route_id = route_04 per refinement chain requirement.

routes.title: Smoothness-Regularized 20-Layer Chirped DBR with Bounded Chirp Envelope
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Adding a gradient smoothness penalty (lambda ~0.1) to the objective function targeting adjacent layer thickness differences will suppress the erratic thickness jumps observed in iteration_13 candidates while preserving the coherent phase-matching structure, leading to improved robustness without sacrificing target score.
routes.design_principle: Chirped dielectric mirror with smoothness regularization to maintain monotonic or gently varying thickness progression that supports broadband reflection in 400-700 nm while maintaining transmission window at 1530-1565 nm.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [HfO2, SiO2] x10 | Fused Silica substrate (20 finite layers total, starting with HfO2)
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds initialized near iteration_13 winning pattern: odd layers 45-90 nm, even layers 65-130 nm with ±10% chirp envelope
theory_basis: Chirped DBR theory for broadband reflection
Regularization theory for smooth optimization trajectories
expected_advantages: Reduced thickness variance improves manufacturing tolerance
Smooth chirp maintains phase coherence across reflection band
Better convergence stability compared to unregularized gradient optimization
known_risks: Over-regularization may trap optimizer in suboptimal local minimum
Smoothness constraint may limit achievable reflection bandwidth
routes.execution_request_english: Design and optimize a 20-layer HfO2/SiO2 chirped dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2 (alternating, 10 pairs, starting with HfO2). Optimize all 20 layer thicknesses using gradient-based optimizer with smoothness regularization penalty (lambda = 0.1) applied to adjacent thickness differences. Initialize thickness bounds: odd-indexed layers (HfO2) 45-90 nm, even-indexed layers (SiO2) 65-130 nm, with ±10% chirp envelope around linear progression. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized or both TE/TM. Spectral bands: 400-700 nm (maximize reflectance), 1530-1565 nm (maximize transmittance). Total layer count fixed at 20. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Added smoothness regularization penalty and chirp-constrained initialization bounds per feedback directives to address erratic thickness jumps in iteration_13 candidates while preserving the ~0.919 target score achievement.

routes.title: 24-Layer Expanded Chirped DBR for Broader Visible Reflection Band
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 20 to 24 layers will broaden the 400-700 nm reflection band coverage while maintaining the 1530-1565 nm transmission window, as additional quarter-wave pairs extend the stopband edges without significantly affecting the telecom band transmission.
routes.design_principle: Extended chirped DBR with more layer pairs to achieve wider reflection bandwidth while preserving transmission at telecom wavelengths through careful thickness distribution.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [HfO2, SiO2] x12 | Fused Silica substrate (24 finite layers total, starting with HfO2)
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness initialization based on iteration_13 winning pattern scaled for 24 layers
theory_basis: DBR stopband width scales with layer count and index contrast
Chirped structures broaden reflection bandwidth beyond periodic DBR limits
expected_advantages: Higher peak reflectance in visible band
known_risks: Increased layer count may reduce 1530-1565 nm transmittance due to cumulative absorption/scatter
More variables increase optimization complexity and risk of local minima
routes.execution_request_english: Design and optimize a 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 chirped dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2 (alternating, 12 pairs, starting with HfO2). Optimize all 24 layer thicknesses using gradient-based optimizer. Initialize thickness bounds: odd-indexed layers (HfO2) 40-95 nm, even-indexed layers (SiO2) 60-140 nm, with linear chirp progression. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized or both TE/TM. Spectral bands: 400-700 nm (maximize reflectance), 1530-1565 nm (maximize transmittance). Total layer count fixed at 24. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Explores whether additional layers (24 vs 20) improve visible band reflection without compromising telecom transmission, testing the layer count vs performance tradeoff within the 30-layer constraint.

routes.title: 20-Layer Chirped DBR with SiO2-First Starting Layer
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Starting the stack with SiO2 (low-index) instead of HfO2 (high-index) will shift the phase relationship at the air-film interface, potentially improving the 1530-1565 nm transmission while maintaining comparable 400-700 nm reflection due to different impedance matching conditions.
routes.design_principle: Inverted starting layer sequence to test phase sensitivity of the chirped DBR structure for dual-band dichroic performance.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [SiO2, HfO2] x10 | Fused Silica substrate (20 finite layers total, starting with SiO2)
manufacturing_considerations: Same thickness bounds as route_04_ref_01 for fair comparison
theory_basis: Fresnel reflection at first interface depends on incident medium to first-layer index ratio
DBR phase conditions sensitive to starting layer index
expected_advantages: Potentially better air-film impedance match for telecom transmission
Tests phase sensitivity hypothesis without changing layer count
known_risks: May reduce visible band reflection due to different standing wave distribution
Could be inferior to HfO2-first configuration
